entries.title: Fruit and the mind
entries.literal_meaning: Fruit grows according to the mind.
entries.explanation: The entry explains the opening as according to one’s mental state or thought. Fruit supplies an image of an outcome. Our reading asks how an attitude shapes the way someone approaches work; it does not claim that thoughts alone control events. Neither success nor suffering can be diagnosed from this short line.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନ ଆରମ୍ଭର କଥାକୁ ନିଜ ମନ ବା ଚିନ୍ତା ଅନୁସାରେ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଫଳ ଏଠି ପରିଣାମର ଛବି ଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମନୋଭାବ କାମକୁ କିପରି ଆଗେଇ ନିଏ, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି; କେବଳ ଚିନ୍ତାରେ ଘଟଣା ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରିତ ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ଦାବି ନାହିଁ। ଏତିକି କଥାରୁ କାହାର ସଫଳତା ବା କଷ୍ଟର କାରଣ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading links outlook with approach, without promising control over results.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମନୋଭାବ ଓ କାମର ଧାରାର ସମ୍ପର୍କ, ଫଳ ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରଣର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରର କାମ ଆରମ୍ଭ ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ଏଥିରେ କିଛି ହେବନି।” ସାଙ୍ଗ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ଫଳ କଣ ହେବ ଜାଣିନି; କିନ୍ତୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟାଟି ମନ ଦେଇ କରିବା।” / Before a reading-group project begins, someone dismisses it. A friend recalls the saying: “I cannot promise the outcome, but let us make a thoughtful attempt.” This exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The following Jagannath Bhagabata verse is a separate literary illustration, not evidence that Jagannath authored this saying. No psychological law, guaranteed reward or blame for hardship is inferred.

entries.title: Do not provoke me
entries.literal_meaning: I am telling you: do not anger me; do not get into it with me.
entries.explanation: The speaker addresses “you” directly, repeating a demand to stop provoking them. The paired endings give the warning its rhythm. Our reading hears a boundary being voiced, without knowing whether the occasion was playful or tense. The source names no quarrel, threat or outcome.
entries.meaning_odia: ବକ୍ତା ସିଧା “ତୁ”କୁ କହି ବିରକ୍ତ କରିବା ବନ୍ଦ କରିବାକୁ ପୁଣି ଦାବି କରୁଛନ୍ତି। ଦୁଇ ଖଣ୍ଡର ମେଳ ଚେତାବନୀକୁ ଛନ୍ଦ ଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଜଣେ ନିଜ ସୀମା କହୁଥିବା ଶୁଣାଯାଏ; ଅବସରଟି ଥଟ୍ଟାର ଥିଲା କି ଉତ୍ତେଜନାର, ଜଣାଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ଝଗଡ଼ା, ଧମକ ବା ପରିଣାମ ଚିହ୍ନାଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A rhythmic direct warning becomes our reading of a spoken boundary.
entries.odia_summary: ସିଧା ଛନ୍ଦମୟ ଚେତାବନୀରେ ନିଜ ସୀମା କହିବାର ଆମ ପଢ଼ା।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ସାଙ୍ଗ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଥଟ୍ଟା କଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ଢଗଟି କହି ଯୋଡ଼ିଲେ, “ମୋତେ ଏହା ଭଲ ଲାଗୁନି; ଏବେ ଛାଡ଼।” ସାଙ୍ଗ କଥାଟି ବନ୍ଦ କଲେ। / A friend repeats a joke. The other invokes the line and adds, “I do not like this; please stop now.” The friend stops. This peaceful outcome is invented, not supplied by the saying.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary labels the quotation Dhaga under causing anger. A voiced warning is retained as its genre; no settled traditional moral or universal rule for resolving conflict is claimed.

entries.title: A meal stretched into a taunt
entries.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: The stool cracks, the navel turns out—only then, Brahmin, rise from your place.
entries.explanation: Cracking furniture and the protruding navel exaggerate a meal into a caste-directed taunt. The final “rise” is retained as an apparent command, rather than silently made a report of what someone did. Our critical reading notices how bodily excess is attached to a named group; it rejects that attachment as evidence of the group’s conduct.
entries.meaning_odia: ଫାଟୁଥିବା ପୀଢ଼ା ଓ ବାହାରୁଥିବା ନାହି ଭୋଜନକୁ ବଢ଼ାଇ ଏକ ଜାତି ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟରେ ଖୋଚା କରେ। ଶେଷର “ଉଠ”କୁ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ଆଦେଶ ଭାବେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି; କିଏ କଣ କଲା ବୋଲି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନାକୁ ବଦଳାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ଦେଖେ କିପରି ଦେହର ଅତିଶୟତା ଏକ ନାମିତ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଏ; ଏହାକୁ ସେ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀର ଆଚରଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ ମାନେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading questions a caste stereotype carried by exaggerated eating.
entries.odia_summary: ଅତିଶୟ ଭୋଜନର ଛବିରେ ଜାତିଗତ ଧାରଣାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠ ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଜଣେ ପୀଢ଼ା ଫାଟିବାର ଛବିରେ ହସିଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଅତିଶୟତାରେ ହସିବା ଓ ଗୋଟିଏ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀକୁ ସେପରି ଭାବିବା ଏକା କଥା କି?” / In a reading discussion, someone laughs at the cracking stool. Another asks, “Is laughing at an exaggeration the same as believing it about a whole group?” This critical exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The source’s bodily gloss explains the image, not a diagnosis. Exact ending syntax remains elliptical; no historical meal, actual person, dietary instruction or customary group behaviour is established.
